newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber steady on government buying support.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber steady on government buying support.

text.p: Thai rubber prices steadied over the week despite slow demand from foreign buyers as the government entered the market again to buy 5,000 tonnes, trade sources said on Wednesday.
The sources added that the government bought 3,500 tonnes of rubber last week at 123.50 US cents and the bidding prices for the latest 5,000 tonnes was at the same level this week.
"They probably bought the rubber to cover government to government obligations or to build stocks," said one trader in southern Hat Yai, Thailand's biggest rubber trading centre.

The Thai government is expected to sign an agreement to sell 20,000 tonnes of rubber with the Netherlands soon. It also last week signed a deal to sell 540 million baht worth of rubber, rice, tapioca and other goods to Mitsui Corp and in exchange for the purchase of 18 billion baht in machinery from the company.
"Otherwise, the market was quiet. Demand from foreign buyers was rather sluggish," said another trader.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for April delivery was quoted around 123 U.S. cents a kg FOB Bangkok and May at $123-124 a kg on the same basis, barely changed from last week.
